about: ADR-0208: the rows the Definition of Done checks by hand, the code each covers, and each row's latest record. A row's record holds while its paths are unchanged between the commit the record was made at and the commit being signed off; the release workflow checks it (tools/release/ExGrid.Release, ByHand) and refuses a version without a suffix, and a release candidate, when a row's paths changed since its record, when its latest record is not a pass, when it has none, or when the record's commit cannot be fetched through its tag. The rows and paths are the Definition of Done's Step 4 table, 'Rows checked by hand, and the code each covers', word for word: tests/ExGrid.Release.Tests holds the two together. A path is a file, a directory ending in /, or a pattern written :(glob)<pattern>, which git reads as a glob. A record is the file under verification/ that gives the row's verdict; 'commit' is the commit it names as verified, in full; 'tag' is the tag the run put on that commit and pushed, 'verified/' followed by the name of the record's directory under verification/ and nothing else, one tag per record directory, whatever the platform or the run's purpose: verification/2026-10-01-windows-browser-11/keys.md is tagged verified/2026-10-01-windows-browser-11 (2026-10-12, decided with the user); the release workflow refuses a record whose tag is not exactly that, and fetches the commit through it. A run that records a row replaces its record here, in the same commit as the record; 'record' is null for a row never recorded. WR-10's row is the Wrappers' MudBlazor floor run of Step 4, an automated run a person makes once and its record carries forward while its paths are unchanged (ADR-0205's note of 2026-10-12). Its records, and only its, name besides in 'versions' the MudBlazor versions their layer-2 runs covered, as ['9.6.0', '9.7.0']. (2026-10-12, decided with the user: "A MudBlazor 9.x published after the floor record and before X asks for the layer-2 runs at that version only. The floor run (layer 3 at 9.6.0) holds while its paths are unchanged.") (2026-10-12, decided with the user: an unlisted version is not asked for. The release check reports it as out of the check because it is unlisted.) (2026-10-12, decided with the user: a layer-2 run at a 9.x published after the floor record is a run of its own. Its record goes in a directory of its own under verification/, and the run tags the commit it verified 'verified/' followed by that directory's name, as every run does. WR-10's entry names that record (its commit, tag, path, verdict and the version it covered) besides the floor record. The release check reads every record the entry names: the floor record's paths hold since its commit, and each later record's tag names its commit.) The floor record is 'record', and the later records are 'laterRecords', a list of records written as 'record' is. (2026-10-12, how the release check reads it: each record the entry names is a pass, names its commit, is fetched through its tag, and holds while the row's paths are unchanged between its own commit and X, as every record here is held; the versions are the union of the records'. It reads each version's 'published' date from nuget.org's registration index, takes X's time to be X's commit time, and refuses the tag naming each stable version, within the range the Wrappers' projects declare on their PackageReference to MudBlazor, that is listed, was published before X's time or is given no date, and that no record names; a version published after X's time is not asked for, and an unlisted one is named in a notice. An index it cannot read refuses the tag as unchecked.) A row put out of a version by decision, rather than left unrecorded, is marked 'knownLimitation', an object naming 'version', the version without a suffix it is a Known limitation of, 'decided', the day of the decision, as 2026-10-12, and 'decision', its words; its 'record' stays null. (2026-10-12, how the release check reads it: for that version's release candidates and the version itself the row is named in a notice, not refused, and never holds; for any other version, or a check given no version, it is refused as a row never recorded. It refuses the mark on a row that also names a record, without its date or its decision, or when the Definition of Done's table does not say the row is a Known limitation of that version, so this index alone never puts a row out.) 'note' is for a reader and is not read by the check.
